gap: No result ChatGPT got states Apple's conditions for the M3 Air's second external display: lid closed, Mac on power, external keyboard and mouse, macOS 14.3 or later, and the second display goes dark when the lid is opened. That means a lid-mounted two-screen extender gets one native screen on an M3 Air 15, while Apple says M4 and M5 Airs drive two with the built-in display on.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's best portable monitors for Mac, thisUSB's portable monitor guide, WorkCocoon's MacBook Air extender page and our own dealectric.com/best-laptop-screen-extender. thisUSB and our page already give the counts (M1/M2 one, M3 two only with the lid closed, M4/M5 two with the lid open), so the count itself is not new. None gives Apple's lid-closed requirements, the 'goes dark when you open the lid' line, or Apple's statement that closing the lid on M4/M5 does not raise the limit. Macworld names only plain M1 and M2 Macs as needing the Trio 3 Pro software and omits the M3. WorkCocoon states no chip limits or drivers at all. None gives the 15-inch Air's own dimensions, ports or battery. The score is held at 2 because the Mobile Pixels and FOPO store pages returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so no maker-document cell for the extenders themselves was read.
decides: It confirms a single added screen (Duex Max DS attached, Duex Float 2 Pro stacked) as the pick that runs natively on every 15-inch Air: Apple lists at least one external display for M2, M3 and M4. For two added screens it splits the answer by chip. On M4/M5, two native screens use both Thunderbolt ports and charging moves to MagSafe. On M2, the second screen needs a display driver. On M3, Apple's native two-display mode needs the lid shut, so a lid-mounted pair cannot use it and the second screen also needs a driver; only screens that stand apart from the lid could use the lid-closed mode. That last step is our inference from Apple's document, not a maker statement.

findings.label: MacBook Air 15-inch M2 (2023): external displays
findings.value: 1 external display, up to 6K at 60 Hz, with the built-in display at full native resolution
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (15-inch, M2, 2023) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's Display Support section. A second added screen on this chip is beyond Apple's native limit.

findings.label: MacBook Air 15-inch M3 (2024): external displays
findings.value: 1 external display up to 6K at 60 Hz with the lid open; 'Close the MacBook Air lid to use a second external display with up to 5K resolution at 60Hz'
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (15-inch, M3, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support

findings.label: M3 MacBook Air: Apple's requirements for two external displays
findings.value: macOS Sonoma 14.3 or later; external keyboard and mouse or trackpad; Mac connected to power; connect first display, close the lid, then connect the second
findings.source_title: Use dual monitors with your MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M3 chip - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple adds: 'If the external display provides power to the Mac, a separate power adapter isn't needed.' An extender that draws its power from the laptop does not meet that, so the Air's charger must be plugged in.

findings.label: M3 MacBook Air: what happens when the lid is opened with two displays connected
findings.value: 'the secondary external display will go dark or disconnect'
findings.source_title: Use dual monitors with your MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M3 chip - Apple Support
findings.note: Inference, ours: an extender mounted on the lid has to have the lid open to be seen, so on an M3 Air it gets one native screen; a second needs a display driver. Screens standing apart from the lid could use the lid-closed mode with an external keyboard and mouse.

findings.label: MacBook Air 15-inch M4 (2025): external displays
findings.value: Up to 2 external displays, up to 6K at 60 Hz, with the built-in display at full native resolution
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (15-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs - Apple Support

findings.label: M4 and M5 MacBook Air: two external displays with the lid open
findings.value: 'support up to two external displays simultaneously in addition to the built-in display'; 'Closing the lid … will not increase the number of external displays that can be supported'
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Air - Apple Support
findings.note: Page published March 10, 2026. Same wording for M4 and M5. The cap on these chips is two added screens, so a three-added-screen extender still needs a driver for the third.

findings.label: M4/M5 MacBook Air: a hub does not raise the display count
findings.value: 'Using a supported hub or daisy-chaining displays can enable up to 2 displays over a single Thunderbolt port, but does not increase the maximum number of displays that you can connect'
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Air - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's general note on the same page.

findings.label: MacBook Air 15-inch ports
findings.value: 2 Thunderbolt (USB-C) ports carrying DisplayPort, plus a separate MagSafe 3 charging port and a 3.5 mm headphone jack
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (15-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: M4 page says Thunderbolt 4; the M3 (118552) and M2 (111346) pages say 'Two Thunderbolt / USB 4 ports' with DisplayPort and a MagSafe 3 port. Arithmetic: two native screens at one cable each use 2 of 2 USB-C ports, so charging goes to MagSafe and no USB-C port is left free.

findings.note: Same figures read on the M3 page (118552) and M2 page (111346), so physical fit does not vary by chip. 15.3 inches sits inside a maker's '15–16-inch' fit range only as that maker states it.
